findings.excerpt: {x ∈ s | #{y ∈ t | G.Adj x y} < (G.edgeDensity s t - ε) * #t}
findings.problem: The private definition `badVertices` has no membership lemma. Its only unfolding is done by passing the definition name to `simp only [..., badVertices, ...]` at line 82, and then a long fragile sequence (`not_and_or`, `not_lt`, `rw [← or_and_left, and_or_left]`, `and_not_self`, `mul_comm (_ - _)`) turns the unfolded filter membership into the needed form. The mathematical statement of membership is not exposed as a rewrite rule, and unfolding the definition leaks the filter shape into every proof that needs it. In `card_interedges_badVertices_le` the same fact is extracted by hand with `(mem_filter.1 hx).2.le`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a private lemma `mem_badVertices : x ∈ badVertices G ε s t ↔ x ∈ s ∧ (#{y ∈ t | G.Adj x y} : ℝ) < (G.edgeDensity s t - ε) * #t := by simp [badVertices]`. Mark it `@[simp]` so `mem_badVertices` fires on `x ∈ badVertices ..` without unfolding the definition. Then use `simp only [mem_sdiff, mem_union, mem_badVertices, ...]` at line 82 and `(mem_badVertices.1 hx).2.le` at line 46. This is a canonical simp lemma for a definition with a pure membership characterization. It would be orientation-safe because the right side contains no `badVertices`.
findings.benefit: The proofs would depend on a stated membership characterization instead of the definition body. The `good_vertices_triangle_card` preamble would be shorter and less sensitive to the exact `simp` normal form. Any later lemma about bad vertices could rewrite membership directly.
